set.audit_note: Spot check Nov 9, 2026: HCD 2024-2028 PLHA NOFA Appendix A lists Napa County (non-entitlement) CY 2024 $219,600 and CY 2025 $241,967, five-year estimate $1,372,500, and City of Napa $223,362 and $239,253. NOFA application deadlines are February 2028 for CY 2024 and February 2029 for CY 2025 funds; plans must prioritize households at or below 60% AMI. prevailing_wage_trigger true is uncited.

reason: HCD PLHA NOFA matches the County and City allocations and the five-year estimate.

set.typical_award_size: City acquires or controls land for affordable development and selects developers by RFP. Current pipeline: the 2.75-acre Jefferson/Trower site at 3875 Jefferson Street (bought 2023; 19 affordable ownership units on a housing land trust model for low and moderate income buyers; developer selected, development phase expected to begin early 2026); The Crescent, 77 deed restricted units on the former County HHSA campus on Old Sonoma Road (first 40 units for low and moderate income households, financing expected to close January 2026 with construction in 2026; AHSC application was not funded). Housing Element Program H2-3.3 had targeted at least 53 low income units on the former Harvest Middle School site (2447 Old Sonoma Road), but the City bought the 26.6-acre site from Napa Valley Unified for $25 million and now lists it as a Future Public Recreation Complex (interim operations since December 13, 2025, long-term vision still to be set), so housing on that site is unconfirmed.
set.next_deadline: Developer RFPs issued as sites become available (Jefferson site RFP released 2024). Watch items: Crescent financing close and 2026 construction start, later Crescent phases seeking state grants, and the City's long-term plan for the City-owned former Harvest Middle School site. Monitor City Council agendas (Legistar client napacity) for RFP notices.
set.audit_note: Spot check Nov 9, 2026: Council Focus Areas page now shows the City purchased the Harvest Middle School site for a public recreation complex, replacing the owner-negotiation framing. prevailing_wage_trigger true is uncited.

reason: Material: typical_award_size and next_deadline described Harvest Middle School as an owner-negotiated affordable site, but the City now owns it as a planned recreation complex.

set.audit_note: Spot check Nov 9, 2026: Ordinance 2026-04 on the City's law library confirms introduction September 1 and adoption September 15, 2026, effective 30 days after passage; 80% bonus and no density cap or three stories/33 feet near major transit for 100% affordable; 65915(v) additional bonus; four incentives at 16% very low or 45% moderate for sale; 15% land donation bonus up to 35% combined; child care bonus; equity sharing on for-sale units; 55-year rental affordability; no required direct financial incentives or fee waivers. The ordinance also amends Chapter 19.28 (inclusionary) and 19.39 (ADUs). prevailing_wage_trigger false is uncited (no public funds).

reason: Ordinance 2026-04 text matches bonuses, incentives, affordability terms and adoption dates.

set.audit_note: Spot check Nov 9, 2026: October 6, 2026 Council staff report on the ADU Fee Assistance Program confirms Measure D (Resolution 2018-072) is restricted to affordable and workforce housing and would fund connection and impact fees for the first three ADUs a year with a 10-year deed restriction at or below 160% AMI, subject to annual appropriation. The report implies Measure D revenue of about $1.03 million a year ($85,500 is 8.3% of annual revenue), roughly double the campaign estimate in the record; proposed annual transfer $85,500 to $217,000. Adoption outcome not confirmed. prevailing_wage_trigger true is uncited.

reason: Staff report matches the restricted use of Measure D and the ADU program terms; newer revenue detail does not contradict the record.
